plan: [This is a one-shot independent private values second-price auction with rational opponents. The dominant strategy is to bid my true value, which maximizes expected profit: I win exactly when my value exceeds the highest competing bid and pay that bid. Overbidding risks paying above value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With no history to learn from and uniform values 0–49, I will bid exactly $31. If there’s a tie at 31, the winner is random and the price equals the tied bid.]

Second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values. The weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value to maximize expected profit. No history and only 1 round, so no scope for learning or signaling. Bidding above risks paying more than my value; bidding below risks losing profitable wins. With 0.1 increments, bid exactly my value. My value is 22, so I will bid 22.

[ In a second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values, bidding one’s true value is a weakly dominant strategy. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth if I win; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With value = 40 and rational opponents likely bidding their values, bidding 40 ensures I win exactly when it’s profitable (when rivals’ highest bid < 40) and pay the second-highest bid. Ties are random; bidding above 40 to break ties could yield negative surplus. For a single round, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit. ]
